Definition: a primary word; to breathe hard, i.e. breeze:--blow. Compare G5594.
BiblicalUsage: Pneo means to blow, as the wind blows. The wind bloweth where it listeth, says Jesus in John 3:8, and so is everyone born of the Spirit. The winds blew and beat upon the house on the rock in Matthew 7:25, and upon the house on the sand in Matthew 7:27 — the same wind, two endings. The sailors hoisted the sail and made for shore in Acts 27:40, and the four winds are held back in Revelation 7:1.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the wind is the Spirit's picture — unseen, sovereign, and free. My position is that I cannot command the wind, but I can be born of it, and built to stand in it.
